source.subject: PHYSICS
source.reasoning_observation: In one nondispersive medium, f_low=50 Hz, f_high=70 Hz and wavelength difference2 m imply v=2/(1/50−1/70)=350 m/s. Musical interval interpreted as frequency ratio.

target.protected_work: Recover a common wave speed from a frequency ratio and signed wavelength difference, then check whether the shared-medium model fits an independent observation.
target.decisive_route: Two tones have f=120 and180 Hz and wavelength difference0.9 m. Find common speed and verify a measured third tone at90 Hz has λ=3.6 m. Shortest valid route: v=324 m/s; wavelengths2.7 and1.8 m; third λ=3.6 m, consistent.

representation_translation.evidence: Translate note ratio into frequencies and signed difference

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Derive speed then both wavelengths and verify

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Frequency and wavelength ratios invert at common speed

core1a.scientific_construction: For two tones in a nondispersive medium, v=f₁λ₁=f₂λ₂. Let r=f₂/f₁>1; then λ₁−λ₂=v(1/f₁−1/f₂)=v(r−1)/(rf₁). The lower frequency has the larger wavelength. Infer speed only if both tones share it; a changed medium or dispersion breaks that constraint. A measured period gives f=1/T, with milliseconds converted to seconds. A third measured wavelength can test the common-speed hypothesis. This source-driven lesson uses distinct original cases.

worked_anchor.task: Two tones have periods10 and5 ms in a medium of speed300 m/s. Find wavelength difference.
worked_anchor.reasoning: f=100,200 Hz; λ=3,1.5 m; difference1.5 m.

core1a.model_limits: Specified ideal or matched conditions only; supplied quantitative relations do not establish compulsory exam scope.

core1b.task: A tone has period8 ms. A second tone has frequency 8/5 times the first. Their wavelengths differ by0.96 m in one uniform nondispersive medium. Recover both frequencies, speed, both wavelengths and predict wavelength of a 250 Hz tone. A reserved measurement is1.30 m exactly; test consistency.
core1b.protected_work: Recover a common wave speed from a frequency ratio and signed wavelength difference, then check whether the shared-medium model fits an independent observation.

stages.predict: Predict which tone has longer wavelength and whether the third observation can independently test the inferred speed.
stages.attempt: A tone has period8 ms. A second tone has frequency 8/5 times the first. Their wavelengths differ by0.96 m in one uniform nondispersive medium. Recover both frequencies, speed, both wavelengths and predict wavelength of a 250 Hz tone. A reserved measurement is1.30 m exactly; test consistency.
stages.reconstruct: f₁=125 Hz, f₂=200 Hz; v=0.96/(1/125−1/200)=320 m/s. λ₁=2.56, λ₂=1.60 m. Third predicted1.28 m; exact1.30 fails common model.
stages.diagnose: Locate any inverted ratio, ms conversion or unjustified shared-speed assumption.
stages.repair: Write the two v=fλ equations, subtract wavelength expressions and check each recovered product.
stages.boundary_test: If third measurement is 1.30±0.03 m, can it alone reject the prediction?

core1b.task: Two tones of frequencies150 Hz and twice that frequency have wavelength difference1.1 m. Infer common speed and both wavelengths. A third tone of period4 ms has observed wavelength1.32 m. Check all observations; state what is conditional if media differ.
core1b.protected_work: Recover a common wave speed from a frequency ratio and signed wavelength difference, then check whether the shared-medium model fits an independent observation.

stages.predict: Predict whether doubling frequency at common speed doubles or halves wavelength.
stages.attempt: Two tones of frequencies150 Hz and twice that frequency have wavelength difference1.1 m. Infer common speed and both wavelengths. A third tone of period4 ms has observed wavelength1.32 m. Check all observations; state what is conditional if media differ.
stages.reconstruct: v=330 m/s; λ=2.2 and1.1 m. Third f=250 Hz, predicted1.32 m. Same-speed hypothesis consistent, not proof of identical conditions.
stages.diagnose: Locate any inverted ratio, ms conversion or unjustified shared-speed assumption.
stages.repair: Write the two v=fλ equations, subtract wavelength expressions and check each recovered product.
stages.boundary_test: If first two tones travel in different media, can difference and frequency ratio alone determine both speeds?

core1b.boundary_response_criterion: No; one difference constrains two unknown speeds.
